static_traits.name: Li Kailing
static_traits.medical_history: No obvious physical illness; no history of similar psychological problems or psychotherapy
static_traits.language_features: Positive attitude, clear expression, fairly good logic, able to self-reflect, highly cooperative

basic_info.main_problem: Because I spent time reading car-related books, I feel obvious guilt, and this guilt has affected my motivation and self-esteem.
basic_info.core_demands: I realize this guilt affects my mental health and my enjoyment of hobbies I once loved, so I seek counseling; I want to enjoy my hobbies again and improve my overall well-being.

core_beliefs: My worth depends on whether I use time on 'more important / more productive' things
Spending time on personal interests is selfish, making me an incompetent mother/wife

special_situations.event: A few days ago, while reading a new book about engine systems
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I spend time on personal interests rather than more productive things or being with family, I am letting my family down
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Sets a strict timetable, limits car-related reading, and forces themselves to turn time toward things deemed 'more useful'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should be doing something more productive/should be with my children; doing this is selfish of me

special_situations.event: Several times a week, when she takes time to read car books alone
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Personal leisure should yield to family duties, otherwise it means I am an incompetent mother/wife
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Shortening or canceling reading time, prioritizing housework and childcare to undo guilt
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am letting them down, I am not good enough

special_situations.event: After work, faces the dual pressure of work and family, when needing to choose between rest and companionship
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Not devoting all time to work and family means failure, with no middle ground
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Sets high standards and tight plans for oneself, reducing personal time to maintain a 'qualified' image
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I cannot relax; relaxing means being irresponsible

special_situations.event: At night before sleep, recalling having spent time reading instead of staying with family
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only maximizing time for family and 'serious matters' counts as competent; other gains do not count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Mentally negating quality time with family that day, using self-criticism to drive less leisure the next day
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Again I did not spend time on what should be done; I am failing

core_conflict.wish: While bearing work and family duties, still being allowed and accepted to enjoy personal interests and self-time, and still seen as a 'good mother/good wife'
core_conflict.fear: Once satisfying self-interests, being seen as selfish and incompetent, harming family relationships and facing criticism or rejection
defense_goal: Maintains the image of a 'qualified caregiver' through self-criticism and raising inner standards
Repressing personal interests and needs to lower the risk of being blamed
Easing guilt and Anxiety with tight planning and excessive responsibility

object_relations.self_representation: A guilty, self-blaming caregiver needing constant self-sacrifice to prove being a 'good person/good mother'
object_relations.object_representation: Family/others who might be hurt or disappointed by me; they will judge me because I focus on myself

object_relations.self_representation: An individual with genuine interests who needs to be allowed
object_relations.object_representation: Internalized 'judge / moral judge' (rules and expectations of society / family)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the topic involves the legitimacy of setting aside personal time for oneself or enjoying reading
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Subconsciously equating allowing the self with harming family, worrying about being seen as selfish and incompetent (transference: projecting the inner 'judge's' gaze onto important others)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Restrained and self-reproaching tone, frequently using 'I should/I should not' phrasing, weakening one's own needs to maintain acceptance.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When feeling relaxed or engaged in personal hobbies, then remembering unfinished family/work tasks
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Understanding inner Anxiety as 'proof I did wrong', believing others will be disappointed or blame oneself
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizing responsibility and efficiency, negating personal interests' value on grounds of 'being more productive', tense tone with self-blame.

manifestations: Experiencing dilemma and inner conflict between personal choices (reading interest) and role duties (mother/wife/employee)
Replacing self-choice with heteronomous 'should/must' standards, difficult to give oneself permission
outcomes: Difficulty relaxing and enjoying interests, decline in sense of well-being
Sleep disrupted, irritability and relationship tension

manifestations: Though having a supportive spouse, not yet expressing true guilt experiences to him
In the family, replaces real communication with self-demands and emotionally isolates herself
outcomes: Lacks external support to regulate emotions, problems are maintained

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Frequently using self-demand statements like 'I should/must be more productive, should accompany the children'
Judging self-worth by external role standards, negating the legitimacy of personal interests

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Repeated self-criticism 'I am not good enough / incompetent'
Shrinking personal time and needs for fear of being judged

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Not communicating true feelings and needs with spouse, instead controlling oneself by limiting reading
Turning the need to seek understanding and support outward into self-repression

positive_force: Has genuine interest and intrinsic motivation in automotive mechanics; can gain satisfaction from learning
Spouse described as a supportive resource
Good self-awareness and willingness to seek help, cooperative positive attitude
Work performance not yet affected, with stable role functioning
Usually also has quality time with family, with a potential foundation for balance
negative_force: Intense 'should/must' rules and perfected role standards
Tending to negate positive evidence and self-achievements (disqualifying the positive)
Strong self-criticism and guilt, oriented toward external evaluation
Avoids expressing inner experience to significant others, leading to absent support
Sleep disturbed and increased stress load, further weakening emotion regulation

target_behavior.behavior: Feels intense guilt and self-blame when doing personal reading (car-related) or thinking about setting aside time for himself
antecedent: After work, when making trade-offs between family and personal time
Recalling the time spent on interests that day before falling asleep
target_behavior.core_reason: Internalized external rules and role expectations ('should be more productive/should give time to family'), equating self-care with selfishness and incompetence
target_behavior.function: Escaping the discomfort of being blamed and guilt by self-criticism and limiting interest activities, maintaining the 'qualified mother/wife' self-image
target_behavior.consequence: Difficulty enjoying interests, decreased motivation, strained relationships with family members, disrupted sleep

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids communicating guilt and true needs with spouse
antecedent: When thinking about discussing the legitimacy of personal time and interests
When feeling guilty or oppressed by self-judgment
target_behavior.core_reason: Worrying self-interests will be judged as selfish, fearing being negated or triggering conflict
target_behavior.function: In the short term avoids shame and feelings of conflict, maintaining superficial harmony and self-image
target_behavior.consequence: Losing real support and empathy, emotions accumulating, relationship tension unresolved
